# Temple Scroll Column 64 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 64:3 — "sojourner" vs. "resident alien" vs. "foreigner" — גר

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sojourner" | Traditional biblical term preserving Hebrew register |
| LOGOS | "resident alien" | Modern scholarly term clarifying legal status |
| PNEUMA | "foreigner" | Accessible but imprecise |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "sojourner." This is an established project convention (see Gen conventions). PNEUMA's "foreigner" conflates גר with נכרי, which are distinct legal categories.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 64:5 — "release" vs. "remission of debts" vs. "cancel debts" — שמטה

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "release" | Literal שמטה |
| LOGOS | "remission of debts" | Technical legal term |
| PNEUMA | "cancel debts" | Plain modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "release" with LOGOS's explanatory phrasing. The Hebrew שמטה means "letting drop" — "release" is closest. PNEUMA's "cancel" is too modern-financial.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 64:7 — "stealing a soul" vs. "kidnapping" — גנב נפש

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "stealing a soul from among his brothers" | Literal גנב נפש |
| LOGOS | "kidnapping any of his brothers" | Clear English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "kidnapping a fellow Israelite" | Dynamic, modern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "kidnapping any of his brothers." "Stealing a soul" (EMET) is opaque; LOGOS retains "brothers" from the Hebrew while clarifying the act. PNEUMA's "fellow Israelite" is adequate but loses the kinship language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 64:8 — "sin worthy of the judgment of death" vs. "crime deserving the sentence of death" vs. "capital crime"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a sin worthy of the judgment of death" | Literal חטא משפט מות |
| LOGOS | "a crime deserving the sentence of death" | Formal legal English |
| PNEUMA | "a capital crime" | Concise modern legal term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a crime deserving the sentence of death." Maintains the gravity of the legal formulation; EMET's "sin" imports theological language where the Hebrew focuses on legal category; PNEUMA is too abbreviated.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 64:9 — "cursed by God" vs. "accursed of God" vs. "under God's curse" — קללת אלהים

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "cursed by God" | Reads genitive as subjective — God does the cursing |
| LOGOS | "accursed of God" | Preserves genitive ambiguity |
| PNEUMA | "under God's curse" | Interprets as objective — the curse relates to God |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "accursed of God." The Hebrew קללת אלהים is deliberately ambiguous — it could mean "cursed by God," "a curse against God," or "an affront to God." This ambiguity fueled centuries of interpretation (cf. Gal 3:13). Only LOGOS preserves it.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 64:11 — "informs against" vs. "acts as an informer" vs. "betrays/acts as a spy" — רכל

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "informs against his people" | Verbal rendering of רכל |
| LOGOS | "acts as an informer against his people" | Noun form, more precise |
| PNEUMA | "betrays his own people by acting as a spy" | Dynamic expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "acts as an informer against his people" with EMET's "delivering" in the next clause. PNEUMA adds "spy" and "treason" as interpretation beyond the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 64:12 — "he shall die" vs. "so that he dies" vs. "let him die there" — interpretation of hanging as execution

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you shall hang him on a tree and he shall die" | Two coordinated clauses |
| LOGOS | "you shall hang him on a tree so that he dies" | Purpose clause — hanging causes death |
| PNEUMA | "you shall hang him on a tree and let him die there" | Adds "there" for vividness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "so that he dies." This is the crux of the column — the Temple Scroll makes hanging the METHOD of execution, not post-mortem display. LOGOS's purpose clause captures this revolutionary legal innovation most precisely. EMET's coordinate clause is ambiguous; PNEUMA adds words not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
